definition: to delay or block by creating an obstacle
memoryTip: Im-pede: put something in the path of the feet — slow progress.
correctPassage: Debris on the track will impede the train’s progress until crews clear it.
wrongPassages: Extra tutors will impede struggling students toward higher scores.
The new express lane will impede rush-hour traffic so cars move faster.
Fresh supplies impede recovery by giving the hospital what it needs.

definition: to gather information bit by bit from various sources
memoryTip: Farmers glean leftover grain — pick up scraps of info the same way.
correctPassage: From scattered letters, historians can glean how the town responded to the crisis.
wrongPassages: She chose to glean the entire archive in one uninterrupted reading.
Investigators gleaned the truth by inventing details no source had provided.
He would glean every document into the shredder before anyone could read it.

definition: lasting only a very short time
memoryTip: Ephemera once meant “for a day” — here today, gone tomorrow.
correctPassage: Social media fame is often ephemeral, fading within a few weeks.
wrongPassages: Stone monuments are ephemeral because they outlast the people who built them.
Their ephemeral friendship has continued through thirty years of weekly letters.
He locked the ephemeral records in a vault marked permanent archive.

memoryTip: In scattered spots — now and then, not on a steady schedule.
correctPassage: The rare bird appears only sporadically along this stretch of coast.
wrongPassages: The factory whistle blew sporadically at the same minute every morning.
She practiced sporadically: two hours every day without missing a session.
Trains arrived sporadically on a published timetable that never changed.

definition: filled with something undesirable; tense with risk
memoryTip: Freighted with trouble — loaded down with tension or danger.
correctPassage: The negotiations were fraught with misunderstandings from the first meeting.
wrongPassages: Their vacation was fraught with calm beaches and uninterrupted sleep.
The simple recipe was fraught with only three ingredients and one pan.
He found the empty hallway fraught with silence and no conflict at all.
